parts.stem:
The grey wolf, *Canis lupus*, is a large predator. During the 20th century, the grey wolf in south-west Europe was hunted almost to extinction.

Fig. 2.1 shows a grey wolf.

{{figure:figure-2-1-source.webp}}

Fig. 2.1
parts.text:
State the genus of the grey wolf.

{{figure:reviewed_response_1.png}}

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Suggest and explain the effects on the biodiversity of south-west Europe if the grey wolf becomes extinct.

{{figure:reviewed_response_2.png}}

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Grey wolves can have territories of up to 950 km². Grey wolves can travel up to 1000 km to start a new population.
parts.text:
State reasons why the mark-release-recapture method is not suitable for estimating the size of a grey wolf population.

{{figure:reviewed_response_3.png}}

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Complete Table 2.1 to show the percentage change in the size of the Iberian grey wolf population from 1970 to 2012.

Write your answer in the table to the nearest whole number.

parts.text:
